scenarios.description: Extraction corruption (INVALID_SOURCE_SPAN-flagged section) + a real resolved amendment targeting that exact section
scenarios.evidence: operative-state.ts never calls index.healthDiagnostics(); computeOperativeContractState returns OPERATIVE_STATE_RESOLVED for a node the index's own health pass had already flagged ERROR/INVALID_SOURCE_SPAN.

scenarios.description: Ambiguous amendment target (duplicate-labeled base section) + amendment effect not yet effective as of the query date
scenarios.evidence: textMissingDespiteAppliedEffect only fires when appliedChain.length>0; with a future-dated effect appliedChain is empty, so status=OPERATIVE_STATE_RESOLVED, currentText=null, unresolvedIssues=[] - indistinguishable from an ordinary unamended provision.

scenarios.description: Amendment target ambiguity via missing definition in the base document + cross-document definition-resolution fallback
scenarios.evidence: operative-state.ts:63's '?? index.getDefinition(group.ref)' fallback (no documentId) resolves to an unrelated document's own definition; provision.currentSourceDocumentId still claims the base document while currentText is the unrelated document's full raw text, with zero unresolvedIssues flagging the leakage.

scenarios.description: Out-of-order amendment ingestion + two amendments sharing an identical effective date
scenarios.evidence: OPERATIVE_STATE_CONFLICTED status is correctly order-independent (GOOD - invariant 21 holds at the status level), but buildProvisionChain's stable sort preserves ingestion-order ties, so currentText differs by ingestion order alone for the identical two real documents - a narrower non-determinism inside an already-flagged CONFLICTED provision.

scenarios.description: Persistence reload + duplicated labels (two colliding-label, distinct-nodeId occurrences, real DB round-trip)
scenarios.evidence: resolveUniquePersistedNodeByRef correctly reports undefined (AMBIGUOUS) both immediately after persisting AND after a genuine fresh-query DB round-trip - no degradation introduced by combining these two conditions.
